claim: Ion conductivity and gating characteristics of tetrameric glutamate receptor ion channels are determined by their subunit composition.
source: Ion conductivity and the gating characteristics of tetrameric glutamate receptor ion channels are determined by their subunit composition.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: Competitive homo- and hetero-dimerization of amino-terminal domains (ATDs) is a key step controlling glutamate receptor assembly.
source: Competitive homo- and hetero-dimerization of their amino-terminal domains (ATDs) is a key step controlling assembly.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The association of kainate receptor ATD dimers is generally weaker than the association of AMPA receptor ATD dimers.
source: The association of kainate receptor ATD dimers is generally weaker than the association of AMPA receptor ATD dimers, but both show a general pattern of increased heterodimer stability as compared to the homodimers of their constituents, matching well physiologically observed receptor combinations.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the measured KD values presented in Tables 1 and 2 and discussed throughout the Results section.

claim: Both AMPA and kainate receptors show a general pattern of increased heterodimer stability compared to the homodimers of their constituents.
source: The association of kainate receptor ATD dimers is generally weaker than the association of AMPA receptor ATD dimers, but both show a general pattern of increased heterodimer stability as compared to the homodimers of their constituents, matching well physiologically observed receptor combinations.
evidence: This is supported by the measured KD values in Tables 1 and 2 showing heterodimers generally have lower KD values than their constituent homodimers.

claim: Signal transduction at excitatory synapses in vertebrate brains is mediated by a large family of glutamate receptor ion channels encoded by 18 iGluR subunit genes.
source: At excitatory synapses in the brain of vertebrates, signal transduction is mediated by a large family of glutamate receptor ion channels (iGluRs) encoded by 18 iGluR subunit genes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: Glutamate receptor ion channels assemble as tetramers.
source: These membrane proteins assemble as tetramers, with coassembly between subunits limited to four major families named AMPA, kainate, NMDA and delta receptors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: There are four AMPA receptor subunits, five kainate receptor subunits, seven NMDA receptor subunits, and two delta receptor subunits.
source: Within each family, there are four AMPA receptor subunits, five kainate receptor subunits, seven NMDA receptor subunits, and two delta receptor subunits, which assemble in different combinations to generate various homomeric or heteromeric species in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: Individual iGluR subtypes and their assemblies exhibit unique gating characteristics.
source: Functional experiments have shown that individual iGluR subtypes and their assemblies exhibit unique gating characteristics (Traynelis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: iGluR tetramers have a modular architecture formed by a layered assembly of extracellular amino terminal (ATD), ligand binding (LBD), transmembrane ion channel (TMD), and cytoplasmic (CTD) domains.
source: These revealed tetramers with a modular architecture formed by a layered assembly of extracellular amino terminal (ATD), ligand binding (LBD), transmembrane ion channel (TMD), and cytoplasmic (CTD) domains (Sobolevsky et al., 2009; Schauder et al., 2013; Karakas and Furukawa, 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Meyerson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to crystal and cryo-EM structures.

claim: The ATD and LBD both combine as dimers with two-fold symmetry.
source: The ATD and LBD, both of which combine as dimers with two-fold symmetry, can be genetically excised and individually expressed as soluble proteins; when crystallized, the soluble proteins form dimeric structures identical to those found in intact receptors (Mayer, 2011; Furukawa, 2012), motivating the study of their assembly using biophysical techniques.
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The ATDs of iGluRs form dimers at low nM to low µM concentrations.
source: By contrast, the ATDs of iGluRs form dimers at low nM to low µM concentrations (Jin et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2009; Karakas et al., 2011; Rossmann et al., 2011), suggesting that ATD oligomerization plays a major role in controlling iGluR assembly.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior analytical ultracentrifugation studies.

claim: ATD oligomerization plays a major role in controlling iGluR assembly.
source: By contrast, the ATDs of iGluRs form dimers at low nM to low µM concentrations (Jin et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2009; Karakas et al., 2011; Rossmann et al., 2011), suggesting that ATD oligomerization plays a major role in controlling iGluR assembly.
evidence: This is inferred from the much stronger binding of ATDs compared to LBDs.

claim: Dimeric GluA2 assembly intermediates have been resolved by single-particle EM studies showing closely apposed ATD domains.
source: In support, dimeric GluA2 assembly intermediates have been resolved by single-particle EM studies after synchronized protein expression, showing closely apposed ATD domains (Shanks et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to EM studies.

claim: ATD interactions are critical for the assembly of functional heteromeric receptors.
source: Further, electrophysiological studies with ATD mutants have shown that ATD interactions are critical for the assembly of functional heteromeric receptors (Kumar et al., 2011; Rossmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to electrophysiological studies.

claim: Additional important contributions in iGluR assembly are likely to arise from the transmembrane domain and auxiliary proteins.
source: On the other hand, additional important contributions in iGluR assembly are likely to arise from other interactions, including the transmembrane domain (Gan et al., 2016), and auxiliary proteins (Jackson and Nicoll, 2011; Sheng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on transmembrane domains and auxiliary proteins.

claim: DyLight 488 and EGFP are labels better suited for FDS experiments on iGluR ATDs than FAM.
source: Using model systems, in subsequent studies we have systematically addressed these issues, identifying DyLight 488 and EGFP as labels better suited for FDS experiments on iGluR ATDs, and have developed analytical procedures and controls that allow measurement of protein interactions with low pM equilibrium dissociation constants (Zhao et al., 2013d, 2013c, Zhao et al., 2014; Chaturvedi et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior work cited in the text.

claim: GluA2 homodimerization has approximately an order of magnitude weaker interaction than initially reported by Rossmann et al.
source: Applied to GluA2 homodimerization (Zhao et al., 2012, 2013d), this revealed approximately an order of magnitude weaker interaction than initially reported (Rossmann et al., 2011), reinforcing the importance of obtaining accurate data to quantitatively study the preferential assembly of iGluR ATDs.
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior measurements compared to earlier published values.

claim: Kainate receptors are encoded by two gene families: GluK1-GluK3 (with 68-75% amino acid sequence identity) and GluK4-GluK5 (with 63% identity but only 25-27% identity with GluK1-GluK3).
source: Kainate receptors are encoded by two gene families, GluK1-GluK3, for which the ATDs share 68–75% amino acid sequence identity; and GluK4-GluK5 which share 63% identity, but exhibit only 25–27% identity with GluK1-GluK3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about kainate receptor sequence relationships.

claim: GluK1-GluK3 form functional homomeric receptors but GluK4 and GluK5 are obligate heteromers which form functional channels only when coexpressed with GluK1-GluK3.
source: GluK1-GluK3 form functional homomeric receptors but GluK4 and GluK5 are obligate heteromers which form functional channels only when coexpressed with GluK1-GluK3 (Perrais et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to functional studies.

claim: GluK1-GluK3 can coassemble to form functional heteromeric kainate receptors.
source: Experiments with recombinant receptors and genetically targeted mice also reveal that GluK1-GluK3 can coassemble to form functional heteromeric KaiRs (Cui and Mayer, 1999; Mulle et al., 2000; Veran et al., 2012) but at present it is not known whether like AMPA receptors these subunits assemble in preferred combinations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: GluK4 and GluK5 ATDs both show a strong preference for heterodimer assembly with GluK1 and with GluK2.
source: By contrast, the GluK4 and GluK5 ATDs both show a strong preference for heterodimer assembly with GluK1 and with GluK2, but with subunit dependent differences in affinity Table 1.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the heterodimer KD values (nM range) to the homodimer KD values (>1 mM for GluK4, 350 µM for GluK5).

claim: GluA4 homodimers show fast interconversion of species on the time scale of sedimentation.
source: By contrast, for GluA4, the peak position shifts to intermediate values at concentrations of 50 and 300 nM — similar to the behavior observed previously for GluA2 (Zhao et al., 2013d) — which is indicative of fast interconversion of species on the time scale of sedimentation (Gilbert and Jenkins, 1956; Dam et al., 2005; Schuck and Zhao, 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the sedimentation patterns in Figure 4B showing concentration-dependent peak shifts.

claim: The measured binding energies of AMPA receptors mirror physiologically observed preferences.
source: The measured binding energies of AMPA receptors, summarized in Figure 7, mirror in many ways physiologically observed preferences, with species of greatest stability being the heterodimers GluA2/GluA3, GluA1/GluA2, and GluA1/GluA3.
evidence: This is inferred by comparing the measured KD values to known physiological receptor compositions.

claim: High affinity heterodimer assembly is not limited to AMPA receptor assemblies containing GluA2.
source: Interestingly, the pairs GluA1/GluA3 and GluA3/GluA4 form heterodimer assemblies of comparable strength to those containing GluA2, indicating that high affinity heterodimer assembly is not limited to AMPA receptor assemblies containing GluA2.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured KD values for GluA1/GluA3 and GluA3/GluA4 being in the same range as GluA2-containing heterodimers.

claim: The comparatively low stability of GluA3 homodimer leads to the strongest preference of GluA3 to hetero-dimerize.
source: In particular, the comparatively low stability of GluA3 homodimer leads to the strongest preference of GluA3 to hetero-dimerize.
evidence: This is inferred from the weak GluA3 homodimer KD (5.2 µM) compared to its heterodimer KD values (1.3-91 nM).

claim: FAM-labeled preparations exhibit a label-induced increase in stability for GluA2 homodimers.
source: Several of the results are in conflict with those obtained in pioneering FDS-SV studies using FAM-labeled preparations (Rossmann et al., 2011) which we have shown exhibit a label-induced increase in stability for GluA2 homodimers (Zhao et al., 2013d).
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior work comparing FAM to other labels.

claim: The present work finds similar affinity for GluA1 and GluA2 homodimers, in contrast to 50-fold difference observed from FAM-labeled preparations.
source: Also, we found similar affinity for GluA1 and GluA2 homodimers, in contrast to 50-fold difference observed from FAM-labeled preparations (Rossmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on comparing the current measurements to prior published values.

claim: GluA2, GluA3, and GluA4 show at least an order of magnitude shorter homodimer lifetime compared to GluA1.
source: In this context we note the new kinetic results which for GluA2, GluA3, and GluA4 show at least an order of magnitude shorter homodimer lifetime as compared to GluA1, seemingly facilitating the pathway to form high-affinity heterodimers.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured koff values for GluA1 versus the other subunits.

claim: AMPA receptors bind more tightly than kainate receptors for both homo- and hetero-dimerization reactions.
source: In general, AMPA receptors bind more tightly for both homo- and hetero-dimerization reactions.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the KD values in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: All kainate receptor homodimers except GluK3 are relatively weak.
source: With the exception of GluK3, all homodimers were found to be relatively weak, which provides larger driving force to form heterodimers among kainate as compared to AMPA receptor ATDs.
evidence: This is based on the measured KD values in Table 1.

claim: Similar guiding principles of subtype combination may exist for other iGluR families.
source: This suggests that similar guiding principles of subtype combination may exist for other iGluR families (Rossmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed patterns in AMPA, kainate, and NMDA receptors.

claim: The GluK3 ATD shows an extremely stable homo-dimer with no dissociation observed even in pM regime.
source: The GluK3 ATD shows an extremely stable homo-dimer with no dissociation observed even in pM regime.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations in Figure 1C.

claim: The gating properties of GluK3 are unique with a low affinity for glutamate and Zn modulation that is absent in other kainate receptors.
source: Interestingly, the gating properties of GluK3 are also unique with a low affinity for glutamate and Zn modulation that is absent in other KaiRs (Swanson et al., 1997; Veran et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on cited functional studies.

claim: Co-assembly of GluK3 with GluK2 has been demonstrated.
source: However, co-assembly of GluK3 with GluK2 has been demonstrated (Cui and Mayer, 1999), indicating that in vivo hetero-dimer formation is possible in spite of the highly thermodynamically favorable homo-dimer.
evidence: This is based on cited experimental work.

claim: EGFP fusion proteins have the advantage of a well-controlled 1:1 labeling ratio.
source: Though not universally applicable, EGFP fusions proteins have the advantage of a well-controlled 1:1 labeling ratio, and do not require laborious and expensive optimization of chemical labeling and associated extra purification steps to remove free dye.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological advantage based on the nature of fusion proteins.

claim: The additional mass of EGFP fusion constructs leads to greater hydrodynamic distinction between homo- and heterodimer species in titration experiments with unlabeled proteins.
source: The additional mass of EGFP fusion constructs also leads to greater hydrodynamic distinction between homo- and heterodimer species in titration experiments with unlabeled proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the physical properties of larger fusion proteins.

claim: DyLight 488 is an inert tag for FDS-SV experiments.
source: These KaiR ATDs were purified and labeled with DyLight 488 as described in Methods and Materials. Avoiding the pitfalls of FAM, DyLight 488 has been shown previously to be an inert tag (Zhao et al., 2013d).
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior work.

claim: GluK1 ATD construct includes mutations G213N/M215T to insert N-linked glycosylation sites.
source: For unlabeled proteins, and for preparations that were later labeled with DyLight 488, the following cDNAs for iGluR ATDs with native signal peptides were cloned into the pRK5-IRES-EGFP mammalian expression vector: GluK1 G213N/M215T, last residue Arg402
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the constructs used.

claim: GluK2 ATD construct includes mutations G215N/M217T to insert N-linked glycosylation sites.
source: GluK2 G215N/M217T, last residue Lys389
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the constructs used.

claim: Mutations in the lateral face of ATD dimer assemblies were introduced to insert N-linked glycosylation sites that prevent protein aggregation.
source: Where indicated, mutations in the lateral face of ATD dimer assemblies were introduced to insert N-linked glycosylation sites that prevent protein aggregation, as reported previously for GluK2 (Kumar et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section and supported by citation.

claim: BSA at 0.1 mg/mL was included in all FDS-SV experiments to minimize surface adsorption of the protein of interest.
source: In all FDS-SV experiments reported in this study, we included 0.1 mg/mL of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in the samples in order to minimize surface adsorption of the protein of interest in the AUC cell.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental procedure in the Materials and methods section.
